items.excerpt: Cleveland Clinic and IBM researchers built Q-CHIPP, a quantum machine-learning framework that predicts which tumor neoantigens will trigger an immune response, outperforming classical methods under data-limited conditions by learning biological patterns from as few as 150 samples on 46 qubits.

A new theoretical framework proposes two scalable quantum-circuit architectures and a parallel training method that mathematically avoids 'barren plateaus,' aiming to make large quantum neural networks trainable while keeping them hard to simulate classically.

Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute researchers found that leading AI protein-structure prediction tools frequently generate physically and chemically impossible results, exposing blind spots and arguing that physics-based molecular-dynamics verification and human oversight remain essential.

A University of Washington Q&A explains how AI now designs and optimizes drug candidates for delivery, stability and pharmacokinetics, tackling the bottleneck in which roughly 90% of candidates never reach the market, tied to a new institute for AI-enabled molecular design.

AI is identifying therapeutic targets faster than ever, but the speed is exposing physical lab bottlenecks and a need for better-quality experimental data to close the loop between AI predictions and validated drug candidates.
